note: Issue 23: a carried RFC 3161 response must commit to the checkpoint head it is attached to. Every verifier (public/verifier.js, verifier/verify.php, the Python package) runs these cases and must agree on each. The two bundles are existing public files, copied byte for byte; nothing was built or signed for this change (see tsa_binding/README.md). The vectors are made by each harness from ONE anchor, the timestamp anchor of the bundle as served, by the edits named below: they are inputs to the binding function only, not bundles.

bundles.what: control C1 of the public planted-defect exchange: the full disclosure exactly as the server served it
PLANTED, defect D7 of the same exchange: the whole bundle minted again under two other keys, with the genuine timestamp response left in place. Its head differs from the head the response commits to.

edits: head: 'other' puts other_head in place of the checkpoint head; 'set:X' puts the string X. digest: 'other' sets the anchor's digest field to other_head; 'absent' removes the field. response: 'truncate:N' keeps the first N bytes of the decoded response; 'append:HH' adds the bytes HH (hex) after it; 'set:X' puts the string X as response_b64; 'absent' removes the field. A missing key leaves that part as served.

vectors.name: response_of_another_head
vectors.head: other
vectors.says: message imprint is for another value
